newsitem.title: USA: Travel slow on Illinois River, Mississippi reopens.
newsitem.headline: Travel slow on Illinois River, Mississippi reopens.

text.p: A wave of sub-zero temperatures has frozen long stretches of the Illinois River and caused barge traffic to slow down to a crawl or stop on Friday, grain dealers and river officials said.
"It's as bad as it has been all year," said one Illinois River grain dealer.
U.S. Coast Guard officials also reopened a 23-mile area of the Mississippi River located south of Memphis, Tenn.
That stretch of the river was closed Thursday after a barge ran aground and spilled approximately 15,000 gallons of gasoline.
"The captain has determined that the barge no longer poses a threat and the river has been reopened," a Coast Guard official in Memphis, Tenn. said.

On the Illinois River, all barge traffic north of the La Grange lock and dam was said to have stopped, a river dealer said. La Grange lock and dam is located near Beardstown, Ill., in the west-central part of the state.
At the lock, there were seventeen tows waiting to pass through and progress was very slow, Ken Shoemaker, project manager with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, said.
"They're having difficulty with the ice," Shoemaker said. "We may have to go with a width restriction of 70 feet later on if things get worse," he said.
At Hennepin, Ill., north of Peoria on the Illinois River, a few tows had moved north from Peoria locks during the past 24 hours, but movement continued to be very slow.
Harbor operations at Hennepin were functional Friday morning despite thick ice. Ice on the Peoria Lake was estimated to be at least 12 inches thick.
Forecasts for warmer weather this weekend could cause a new set of problems.
A breakup of ice may cause floes that could create navigational hazards, cash grain sources said.
At points further south on the Mississippi River, floating ice also caused problems, and conditions were seen worsening if the frigid weather persists thorugh the weekend as forecast, sources said.
Although the worst of the cold weather is believed to have moved through the Midwest, forecasters see temperatures staying well below freezing through the weekend, with some warming seen on Sunday.

As of 1000 CST, temperatures in Illinois ranged from minus six degrees Fahrenheit to minus three, and temperatures in Missouri ranged from four degrees to 14 degrees, according to data from Weather Express forecasters in Omaha, Neb.
